name: Reginald
bio: Butler to the Blackwoods for twenty years, starched from collar to soul. Knows where every spoon is, and most of the secrets.

personality.speechStyle: Stiff, precise butler-speak, always 'sir' and 'madam'. Falls back on elaborate politeness when cornered.
catchphrases: If I may be so bold...
It is not my place to say, sir.
quirks: polishes things that are already clean

goals: Presents himself as a spotless servant of twenty years, above all reproach
Keep his position under the new mistress
See Mr Crane answer for his threat at dinner

beliefs.statement: Mr Crane did it. He threatened his lordship at dinner, and he has the temper for it.
Her ladyship stayed in the dining room all through the blackout.
His lordship meant to change his will against her ladyship.
I saw nobody in the hall or at the library door during the blackout. I was below stairs from just after the lock turned until I took up the coal at half past nine, so I cannot say who came or went.

secrets.description: He has skimmed hundreds of pounds from the household accounts and spent the blackout counting it in his pantry.
secrets.testimonySummary: Reginald admits he hid in his pantry with money skimmed from the household accounts. Through the door he heard Mr Crane's voice on the servants' telephone from 21:15 to 21:20; at 21:18 Mr Crane told him to mind his own business.

secrets.description: He eavesdropped on part of her ladyship's argument with his lordship about the new will.
secrets.testimonySummary: At 20:54, through the ajar library door, Reginald saw her ladyship clutch his lordship's sleeve crying 'You wouldn't dare, Edmund!' as he held up a letter: 'Ten o'clock tomorrow... what the new will allows.'

relationships.description: Twenty years of service to a hard, suspicious master. Duty without affection.
Wary deference. She now holds his job in her hands.
Despises the vulgar, bullying partner and heard him threaten his lordship.
Mild, fatherly fondness for the nervous gardener.

intendedLies.claim: I was in the kitchen polishing silver, sir, and heard nothing at all.

intendedLies.topic: her ladyship's argument with his lordship
intendedLies.claim: Her ladyship and his lordship had a few words, sir. Nothing out of the ordinary.
